assessment.reason: The under depends on a heavily shrunk assist rate. Recent sourced form and power-play production point the other way, and only one other book quotes this line.
assessment.model_case: The projection is about 0.28 assists against a 0.5 line. That low mean appears driven by shrinkage toward a long 164-game history. Recent output and power-play involvement suggest the shrinkage may be understating his current role.

assessment.context_case: Dated reporting describes a five-game point streak and heavy power-play production. If that role continues, his assist chances would sit well above the model mean. Power-play assignment remains unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: Point streaks often regress. The model's long sample may properly discount an 11-game surge, and an under on a single assist can still win at a decent rate for a middle-six winger. If he has been moved off the top power-play unit, the case could look closer to the model.

qualitative_review.countercase: A one-shot median against a 1.5 line can flip with a promotion or extra power-play time. Winnipeg injuries could shift Vilardi's deployment upward. The market may be pricing role information this model lacks, and the gap from two books warrants caution.

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 341 points against 304 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.
